question: By selling an article at (3)/(11) of its marked price, Hitesh incurs a loss of 15%. If he sells it at 54% of its marked price, then the profit percentage is
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use 100 base:

⇒ Loss 15% ⇒ CP = 100, SP = 85

⇒ SP = 3/11 MP ⇒ 85 = 3/11 MP ⇒ MP = (85 × 11) ÷ 3

⇒ New SP = 54% MP = 0.54 × (85 × 11 ÷ 3)

⇒ SP = 168.3, CP = 100

⇒ Profit = 68.3%

**∴ Answer ≈ 68.3%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

SP = (3 ÷ 11) MP

Loss = 15%

**Concept Used:**

Loss% = [(CP − SP) ÷ CP] × 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let MP = 11

⇒ SP = 3

⇒ Loss = 15%

⇒ SP = 85% of CP

⇒ 3 = 0.85 CP

⇒ CP = 3 ÷ 0.85 = 60 ÷ 17

⇒ New SP = 54% of MP

⇒ = 0.54 × 11 = 5.94

⇒ Profit% = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100

⇒ = [(5.94 − (60 ÷ 17)) ÷ (60 ÷ 17)] × 100

⇒ ≈ 68.3%

**∴ Profit ≈ 68.3%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Loss Formula:** SP = CP × (1 − Loss%)

**Profit Formula:** Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

**Ratio Trick:** Assume convenient base (100) for percentage problems

**Shortcut Tip:** Convert fractions and percentages into simple numbers
